overall: The AG found the cooperative's executive session topic descriptions sufficient and most other claims unfounded, but found violations for a six-day minutes-release delay, apparent lapses in periodic minutes review, and two executive session procedure failures; ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the electric cooperative failed to name executive session topics or give adequate specificity, relying on Purpose 10 descriptions.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, in the instances at issue in this complaint, a description of this type was sufficient to meet the standards of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected to the body's use of acronyms in meeting minutes and notices.
allegations.key_passage: While we do not consider CVEC's use of acronyms here to be a violation, we generally discourage public bodies from using acronyms in meeting minutes because members of the public may not understand the meaning of such abbreviations.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the body waited too long to release executive session minutes after a February 2014 request, beyond the 10-day response window.
allegations.key_passage: we find that CVEC violated the Open Meeting Law by waiting six days before releasing the minutes that it determined could be released during the February 27, 2014 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the body failed to periodically review executive session minutes, with some minutes nearly four years old before review.
allegations.key_passage: suggests that CVEC was not periodically reviewing executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that minutes show the body entered executive session without first convening in open session (March 2012) and without stating whether it would reconvene (April 2011).
allegations.key_passage: These failures constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 5, 2013 notice listed two executive session topics but four or more were actually discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find the notice was sufficient and there was no violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Executive Committee discussed Cape Wind on August 19, 2010 without a properly noticed meeting or minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, this appears to have been merely an administrative error

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a pattern of failure and a systematic effort to deprive the public of information across many meetings.
allegations.key_passage: As a general policy, we do not review generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complainant's claims covered events before July 1, 2010, when the Attorney General assumed Open Meeting Law enforcement.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to consider claims regarding events that occurred prior to July 1, 2010.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
